User guide

What's new

The program shows the section of its own version in the welcome window. One section per month, newest first.

kt26.11

  • Ctrl+F shows what it finds again. The search window kept the height of its empty field, so the media, events and markers it found were hidden under its bottom edge until you dragged the window larger.
  • Opening a project with a reel no longer asks to save changes you did not make. Once the reel's preview had drawn on the timeline, opening another project or quitting asked "save your changes?" about a project nobody had touched, and quitting left a recovery file behind.
  • Rendering a region no longer closes the program at 100 %. A render of a region that does not start exactly on a frame — any region drawn by hand, even 0.2 s — used to reach 100 % and take the whole program down, sometimes with the file half-written. It now finishes, shows its summary and closes like any other.
  • A camera you can film your frame with: Camera ISP. The new effect undoes the camera that made your footage back into a scene, then films it again with a simulated camera: a lens (defocus, distortion, chromatic aberration, vignetting, colour shading), a colour mosaic (RGGB and its phases, Quad Bayer, X-Trans, RGBW, RGB-IR with infrared pixels), a sensor that counts electrons with their real noise, blooming and banding, and the camera's processor with a block for every one of those defects — black level, row/column correction, defect pixels, green balance, raw denoise, lens shading, white balance, demosaic, distortion and colour-fringe correction, colour matrix, tone curve, denoise, sharpening and YUV with 4:2:0. Every block can be switched off or set wrong, "View" shows the picture after any stage, and the looks follow from it: "Phone at night", "Cheap webcam", "Security cam, IR", "Cinema raw", "Wrong CFA phase", "No IR-cut filter". The noise is the same on every play and render.
  • A real start window. The welcome window has three columns — Start (the tour, templates drawn in their frame's shape, the five lessons with your progress), Recent (your projects with their pictures, as many per row as fit) and What's new, now readable in its own column. Each column scrolls on its own, and the window can be made as large as the screen.
  • File → Preferences… holds the program's settings. Language, Economy UI, whether the welcome window opens at start, the usage statistics, the daily update check and FFmpeg are in one window, each switch in one place; the View menu keeps only what changes the view.
  • The language you chose stays chosen. Opening another project used to forget it, and the next start came up in the system language; Economy UI was forgotten the same way.
  • A real VHS: the tape is written and read back. The new VHS Tape effect does not paint stripes on the picture — it records it as a VHS deck does (the brightness on an FM carrier, the colour on a low "colour-under" carrier, two heads on a spinning drum writing slanted tracks) and plays the tape back. Snow, colour smear, the noise bar, the tear at the bottom and wobbly lines come out of the causes: click a head on the drawn drum and make it dirty, clogged or chipped, turn the tracking, switch SP/LP, a TBC, four heads for a clean pause, or record on one deck and play on another. The old VHS look is still there.
  • Datamosh — a real one. The new Datamosh effect runs its own little video codec over the clip — motion search, a prediction loop, quantised detail, keyframes — and lets you break it on purpose: drop the keyframes so the previous shot gets dragged by the new shot's motion, repeat one frame's motion until it blooms, freeze the reference, scale, turn or swap the motion vectors, borrow the motion of the clip on the track above or below, lose detail or whole blocks. The breakages take curves: switch the mosh on and off, or put a Reset key on the beat to start clean from that frame. Presets: Cut mosh, Bloom, Transplant, Melt. Any frame looks the same when you play up to it, jump to it or render it.
  • Masks. Right-click the picture → Mask → Rectangle, Ellipse or Pen, and draw right over the preview: the pen makes a Bézier path (click — a corner, click and pull — a smooth point). Each mask has feather (smooth or linear), expansion, opacity, invert and a mode — add, subtract, intersect, difference — and several masks combine from the top down. A mask on the event's picture follows the event when you move, scale or rotate it; an effect can be limited to its own masks (under its parameters in the effects window) — a blur on a face, a colour only in a corner; a track can be masked from its window. The stopwatch on a mask animates its whole shape: drag a point at another moment and the shape is keyed there.
  • Composition previews no longer get rebuilt by chance when a project opens. Opening a project sometimes found its own index file "busy" and drew the frames and waveform of every composition all over again; now the saved previews come back every time.
  • Diagnostics holds all of Performance, with three graphs. The Performance box no longer sits under the media bin — the bin gets the whole column. The gauge button (or View → Diagnostics…) opens one window with every number the box had and three graphs side by side in time: playback, FFmpeg activity and the cache. Make the window larger and the graphs grow.
  • Sound generators: tone, noise, sweep, beeps and silence. Edit → Create a generator → Audio puts a line-up tone, white/pink/brown noise, a sine sweep, a train of sync beeps or a stretch of silence on an audio track. Levels are in dBFS (−20 dBFS of tone and of noise read the same on the meters), a tone or a beep can go to one channel, and the sound is the same on every play, seek and render.
  • "Create a generator" left the File menu. It is in Edit now, and in a track's right-click menu, which puts the generator exactly where you clicked — a video track offers the picture kinds, an audio track the sound kinds. The media bin keeps its item.
  • Every window can be made bigger, and what is inside grows with it. Drag a window's corner: the effects chain, the curve graph, the lists, the Guide and the render log take the new room instead of leaving an empty frame around a small box. Each window remembers the size you gave it — an effects window opens as large as the last one you enlarged.
  • The Guide reads like a manual. Its tables are real tables, with a shaded header, lines between the cells and a key column as wide as its keys; every "I want to…" entry is its own card, the place to act written under it.
  • Adding an effect shows one big gallery. The "+ effect" picker is as wide as its window and as tall as the screen allows — presets first, then the effects — with more thumbnails per row in a wider window.
  • No button is cut off at the end of the toolbar. In a narrow window the buttons that do not fit (Render, Search, Diagnostics, Save…) move into a ⋯ menu at the end of the row.
  • Zigzag and the other segment shapes on one piece of a curve, or on a hundred. Right-click a segment, or Ctrl+click several, or drag across empty space in the curve graph: under "Shape of all segments" a row appears with the same fields for just those segments. Values that differ show "—"; a typed number sets all of them, dragging the field shifts each by the same amount.
  • Windows: the welcome window names your project folders plainly — C:\Users\…, not \\?\C:\Users\….
  • A project sounds and looks the same on Windows and Linux. Slowed+Reverb, the phaser and pitch shift gave slightly different bytes on Windows; every effect now uses the program's own math, so a render is identical on both — and on any processor.
  • Forcing an encoder this computer does not have (VAAPI on Windows) now says so by name instead of an empty error.
  • If Kinetren crashes, a window says so at once — the error, the version and the last lines of the log, with Restore the project and Open the log folder. Before, you learnt it only at the next start, if at all.
  • Restoring after a crash brings back your own footage. The restored project no longer plays a lesson's test patterns in place of your sources, and keeps its own name.
  • Rendering a region that does not start on a frame no longer closes the program.
  • The log keeps one file per run (the four previous runs next to it), each starting with the version and the start time in your time zone.
  • The tour points where to act. Every lesson step outlines its place — the menu item, the event, the marker, the button in a window — and Show scrolls to it or opens its menu instead of doing the step for you. Keys and buttons in the lesson text are drawn as keycaps.
  • The tour no longer lags or misleads. "Play a part in a loop" counts the moment the loop is on, even with a window open; the transitions lesson teaches Transition with previous (an overlap stays a cut); after an effect or a transition the lesson says what changed and moves the playhead to where you can see it. "Next lesson" no longer asks to save the lesson's own copy, the lessons panel no longer hides the right end of the toolbar, and the render lesson tells silly jokes while it waits.
  • Click a marker on the ruler to put the playhead on it.
  • Pitch no longer tears between short events. Cut an event with pitch into many short pieces and they sound exactly like the uncut event; any pitched event starts and ends without a dip — also when the pitch comes after Slowed+Reverb or an echo, or from a morpher.
  • Changing an audio effect takes effect at once. Put a filter where an equaliser stood and you hear the filter right away — before, the old effect kept playing with the new settings until you jumped in time.
  • The strength slider in the effects gallery no longer mixes the settings of two different effects.
  • Every effect, transition and generator is now a plugin inside — blur, glow, VHS, noise, the chroma key and the rest moved too. Your projects open and look exactly as before.

kt26.10

  • Windows. A portable Windows build; FFmpeg is found on the computer or downloaded with one click.
  • FFmpeg 9 works, as do 6, 7 and 8.
  • Under wine the interface is dark everywhere and our own title row is back.
  • A quiet reminder about updates. Once a day the program checks whether a newer release is out and says so in the bell — no pop-ups.
  • A welcome window at start. New projects from templates, the recent projects with a frame of each, the tour and this page. One tile is highlighted: Enter takes it. Switch the window off with Show at start; Help → Welcome window… brings it back.
  • The tour. Short lessons on a demo project made of generators. A step closes by itself when the project shows it done — see Getting started.
  • Help → Guide… finds where a thing is done: type what you want, or open a page of this guide.
  • One window shell. Every window closes by its cross and by Esc, the top one first, and no window grows by itself.
  • The render window names the encoder before the first frame, counts the bytes and asks before replacing a file.
  • The FFmpeg window tells what it downloads, where it goes, how fast, and why.
  • Effects are plugins inside. The built-in effects moved into their own crates behind one interface; projects keep their bytes.
  • Faster event grids. A grid computes one cell and copies it; a morpher layer at strength zero costs nothing.
